name: pdwrite
description:
A ProDOS VOLUME MOUNTED WITH -o write IS WRITTEN AS ProDOS 8 WOULD WRITE IT, AND OTHER READERS AGREE.  /dev/sd1 is disk/pdscratch.po; /testdata/pdwrite writes through pdmount -p/-A/-P and the check script reads the volume the machine left.

ON THE SCREEN:
  mw=0      mount -o write mounted writable.
  PDWR hello 600   a seedling written past its first block: promotion to sapling.
  PDWR sap 120000  a sapling grown past 256 blocks: promotion to tree.
  PDWR sap 100     a write into the sapling's holes.
  PDWR tree 700    an overwrite of existing blocks.
  PDWR ext 1000    a GS/OS extended file's data fork grows.
  PDWR ._ext 0 errno=1   the resource fork file is not written: EPERM.
  PDWR f01 5       O_APPEND lands at the EOF.
  PDWR sub/inner/deep 5000   a file two directories down, whose writes ripple.
  PDWR f03 open errno=13  uid 1 cannot open a 0644 root-owned file for write.
  PDWR sub open errno=21  a directory cannot be opened for write.
  PDCR NewFile.Txt errno=0   a file is created in the volume directory.
  PDCR a_b errno=22        a name ProDOS cannot hold: EINVAL.
  PDCR HELLO errno=17      O_EXCL on a name that exists, whatever its case: EEXIST.
  PDCR ._ext errno=1       the resource fork file is never created: EPERM.
  PDCR sub/nope errno=13   uid 1 cannot name a file in a 755 root-owned directory.
  PDMK sub/NewDir errno=0  a directory is made in a subdirectory; PDMK sub errno=17.
  PDWR NewFile.Txt 700     the new seedling grows into a sapling.
  PDCN f 20 errno=0        twenty files in the new directory, which grows a block.
  cwd=/mnt/sub/NewDir      pwd climbs out of it by inode number and name.
  PDCN v N errno=28        creating until the volume directory is full: ENOSPC.
  PDWR f09 N errno=28     writing until the volume is full ends in ENOSPC.
  PDWR /mnt/f04 open errno=30  a read-only remount refuses a write open.
  um=0 ro=0  both unmounts succeed.

IN THE CHECK SCRIPT (pdwrite_check.py): cadius CHECKVOLUME silent (after a control it must flag), cadius EXTRACTVOLUME byte-identical to the writes replayed on the generator's contents, each written entry's storage type, blocks used, backup bit and date, with the ripple re-dating SUB and INNER, each created entry's fields, and every directory's file count, parent pointers, block chain and entry size.
